title: Market Surf Report

conditions.headline: Choppy Water After the Chip Wipeout
conditions.summary: Futures are modestly lower after Thursday's steep tech and chip selloff, with oil near $101 on Iran tensions. Bonds rallied, pulling the 10-year yield below 5%.

sections.title: Futures & Overnight
items: S&P 500 futures -0.2%, Nasdaq-100 futures about flat, Dow futures -0.6%, Russell 2000 futures -0.5% (early quotes, around 6 AM ET).
Thursday: S&P 500 -1.2%, Nasdaq-100 -2.9%, Dow flat; the Philadelphia chip index fell 6.7%, its worst day since June, after Meta raised AI spending plans.
WTI crude +1.6% near $101 and Brent near $113–114 on reports of more US and Israeli strikes on Iran.
The 10-year Treasury yield fell to about 4.95%, its first close below 5% in a month, as investors sought safety in bonds.
Gold slipped below $4,000; bitcoin near $81,700; VIX up near 19.7.
Asia: Nikkei slipped, Kospi recovered from a near-4% drop to about flat, China's CSI 300 rose; Taiwan was closed for a typhoon.
Europe: Stoxx 600 lower as French 10-year yields hit a 24-year high above 5.1% on budget worries.

sections.title: Macro & Economic Calendar
items: 8:45 AM CT: S&P Global flash PMIs for October — services forecast 57.9 (prior 58.8), manufacturing 55.4 (prior 55.9).
9:00 AM CT: University of Michigan final October sentiment — forecast 46.3 (prior 48.1); 1-year inflation expectations forecast 4.7%.
The Fed's next decision is Wednesday, Oct 28; traders price roughly an 80% chance of a hike by December as oil feeds inflation worries.
Thursday's jobless claims fell to 194,000, a historically low level.

sections.title: Earnings
items: Western Digital beat fiscal Q1 estimates and gave an upbeat outlook, but shares are down about 2% pre-market.
Bloom Energy is down about 2% more after a nearly 9% drop Thursday on capex and cash flow concerns.
RingCentral +15% pre-market after beating Q3 estimates and raising full-year guidance; MaxLinear +10% on upbeat results.
Deckers Outdoor -9% after mixed results and a fiscal 2027 sales outlook below estimates.
American Express and SLB report before today's open; a light after-the-close slate. Alphabet and Microsoft report next Wednesday.

sections.title: Stocks in the News
items: RNG (RingCentral): +15% — Q3 beat and raised guidance.
CCI (Crown Castle): +7% — Bloomberg says SpaceX is in talks to secure 80,000+ US cell sites; American Tower (AMT) +6%.
VZ, T, TMUS (Verizon, AT&T, T-Mobile): -3%+ — the SpaceX wireless-carrier report weighs on carriers.
MRNA (Moderna): -4% — extends Thursday's ~18% slide after its melanoma vaccine data leaked early.
DECK (Deckers Outdoor): -9% — cut fiscal 2027 sales guidance below estimates.
SKHY (SK Hynix): +5% — halted its review of a pre-IPO raise for its US unit Solidigm.
CRWV (CoreWeave): +2% — bouncing after a 10% drop to a 17-month low on debt worries.
META (Meta Platforms): -0.6% — extends a 7% drop on higher AI spending and a planned share sale.

sections.title: Business News
items: SpaceX and Tesla have each formed special committees of independent directors to study a combination; reports point to a 2027 announcement target.
Reports say investors pushed OpenAI to trim its fundraising valuation target to $1.25 trillion from $1.4 trillion.
Meta plans to issue new shares to help fund AI spending after guiding 2026 capex to $135–145 billion.
Oil near five-month highs after reports the US is prepared for a long fight with Iran.
London Stock Exchange Group jumped about 8% after raising its revenue outlook.

sections.title: What to Watch Today
items: 9:00 AM CT: Michigan sentiment and inflation expectations.
Oil around $100 WTI and the 10-year near 4.95%.
Whether chip stocks stabilize after Thursday's 6.7% index drop.

script: Cowabunga! This is Surf Daddy, your local Kahuna, live from Surfside USA to all you Trade Wind surfers from the Gulf Coast to the North Shore. It's Friday, October twenty-third, twenty twenty-six, and this is your Market Surf Report. Riding shotgun in the cabana this morning, with sand on his paws and his ears up, is Gus the wonder dog. Gus, give the Dawn Patrol a howdy! Let's check the swell. After Thursday's gnarly tech wipeout, futures are choppy. S and P futures are down two tenths of a percent, Nasdaq futures are flat, the Dow is off six tenths, and the Russell is down half a percent. These are early quotes. Thursday the chip index sank almost seven percent, its worst day since June, after Meta raised its AI spending plans. Oil is the big current. West Texas crude is up one and a half percent, near one hundred and one dollars, on reports of more strikes on Iran. The ten year yield slid to about four point nine five percent as traders paddled to bonds. Gold is just under four thousand dollars, bitcoin is near eighty one thousand seven hundred, and the VIX is near nineteen and a half. Overseas, Tokyo slipped and Seoul recovered to flat. Europe is lower, with French yields at a twenty four year high. Wind and weather. Flash readings on manufacturing and services land at eight forty five A M Central. Michigan consumer sentiment follows at nine A M Central, expected near forty six. The Fed meets next Wednesday, and traders lean toward a hike by December. On the tide chart, Western Digital beat and guided higher, but it is still down two percent. American Express and S L B report before the bell. In the lineup, RingCentral is up fifteen percent after a beat and a raised outlook. Stoked! That calls for a treat, Gus! Here you go, buddy! Crown Castle and American Tower are up six to seven percent on a report that SpaceX wants tens of thousands of cell sites to become a wireless carrier. Verizon, AT and T, and T Mobile drop three percent. Moderna is down four percent after leaked melanoma vaccine data sparked an eighteen percent drop Thursday. Deckers is down nine percent on a weak outlook. Beach talk. SpaceX and Tesla formed committees to study combining. Reports say OpenAI's valuation target was trimmed, and Meta plans new shares to fund its AI build. Sets to watch: sentiment at nine Central, oil near one hundred dollars, and whether chips find their footing. No need to drop in on the first choppy wave. Soul Surfers wait for a clean set. This is Surf Daddy and Gus the wonder dog saying, if in doubt, paddle out!
